# zgtrfs

> Improves the computed solution to a complex system A * X = B where A is.

<section class="intro">

tridiagonal and provides error bounds.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zgtrfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zgtrfs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zgtrfs(
    order,
    trans,
    N, nrhs,
    DL, strideDL,
    d, strideD,
    DU, strideDU,
    DLF, strideDLF,
    DF, strideDF,
    DUF, strideDUF,
    DU2, strideDU2,
    IPIV, strideIPIV,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    RWORK
) → info: integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | 'no-transpose', 'transpose', or 'conjugate-transpose' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand side columns |
| `DL` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | sub-diagonal of A (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DL (complex elements) |
| `d` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | diagonal of A (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for d (complex elements) |
| `DU` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | super-diagonal of A (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DU (complex elements) |
| `DLF` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | factored sub-diagonal from zgttrf |
| ↳ `strideDLF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DLF (complex elements) |
| `DF` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | factored diagonal from zgttrf |
| ↳ `strideDF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DF (complex elements) |
| `DUF` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | factored super-diagonal from zgttrf |
| ↳ `strideDUF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DUF (complex elements) |
| `DU2` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 2` |  | second superdiagonal from zgttrf |
| ↳ `strideDU2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DU2 (complex elements) |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in | `N` |  | pivot indices from zgttrf (0-based) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IPIV |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of B (complex elements) |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix, refined on output |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of X (complex elements) |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output forward error bounds |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output backward error bounds |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BERR |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | workspace |
| `RWORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | real workspace |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `DL`: The (n-1) subdiagonal elements of A.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) superdiagonal elements of A.
- `DLF`: The (n-1) multipliers that define the matrix L from the LU factorization of A as computed by ZGTTRF.
- `DF`: The n diagonal elements of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A.
- `DUF`: The (n-1) elements of the first superdiagonal of U.
- `DU2`: The (n-2) elements of the second superdiagonal of U.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le i \le n$, row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`. `IPIV(i)` will always be either i or i+1; `IPIV(i) = i` indicates a row interchange was not required.
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by ZGTTRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` twenty-second argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-second argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-fourth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-fourth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zgtrfs.ndarray(
    trans,
    N, nrhs,
    DL, strideDL, offsetDL,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    DU, strideDU, offsetDU,
    DLF, strideDLF, offsetDLF,
    DF, strideDF, offsetDF,
    DUF, strideDUF, offsetDUF,
    DU2, strideDU2, offsetDU2,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → info: integer
```

Improves the computed solution to a complex tridiagonal system and provides error bounds.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | specifies the form of the system |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand side columns |
| `DL` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | sub-diagonal of original A (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DL (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for DL (complex elements) |
| `d` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | diagonal of original A (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for d (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for d (complex elements) |
| `DU` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | super-diagonal of original A (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DU (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for DU (complex elements) |
| `DLF` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | factored sub-diagonal from zgttrf (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDLF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DLF (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDLF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for DLF (complex elements) |
| `DF` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | factored diagonal from zgttrf (length N) |
| ↳ `strideDF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DF (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for DF (complex elements) |
| `DUF` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 1` |  | factored super-diagonal from zgttrf (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDUF` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DUF (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDUF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for DUF (complex elements) |
| `DU2` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N - 2` |  | second superdiagonal from zgttrf (length N-2) |
| ↳ `strideDU2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for DU2 (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDU2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for DU2 (complex elements) |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in | `N` |  | pivot indices from zgttrf (0-based) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IPIV |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for IPIV |
| `B` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix (N x NRHS) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of B (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of B (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for B (complex elements) |
| `X` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix (N x NRHS), refined on output |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of X (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of X (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for X (complex elements) |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output forward error bounds (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for FERR |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output backward error bounds (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BERR |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for BERR |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | workspace of length >= 2*N complex elements |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for WORK (complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | real workspace of length >= N |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for RWORK |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | offset for RWORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose)
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `DL`: The (n-1) subdiagonal elements of A.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) superdiagonal elements of A.
- `DLF`: The (n-1) multipliers that define the matrix L from the LU factorization of A as computed by ZGTTRF.

- `DUF`: The (n-1) elements of the first superdiagonal of U.
- `DU2`: The (n-2) elements of the second superdiagonal of U.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices; for $1 \le i \le n$, row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`. `IPIV(i)` will always be either i or i+1; `IPIV(i) = i` indicates a row interchange was not required.
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by ZGTTRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix X.

If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zgttrf from './../../zgttrf/lib/index.js';
import zgttrs from './../../zgttrs/lib/index.js';
import zgtrfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zgtrfs';

const n = 4;
const DL = new Complex128Array( [ 2, 1, 1, -1, 3, 0.5 ] );
const d = new Complex128Array( [ 4, 1, 5, 2, 3, 1, 6, -1 ] );
const DU = new Complex128Array( [ 1, 0.5, -1, 1, 2, 1 ] );
const DLF = new Complex128Array( [ 2, 1, 1, -1, 3, 0.5 ] );
const DF = new Complex128Array( [ 4, 1, 5, 2, 3, 1, 6, -1 ] );
const DUF = new Complex128Array( [ 1, 0.5, -1, 1, 2, 1 ] );
const DU2 = new Complex128Array( n );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( n );
const B = new Complex128Array( [ 5, 1.5, 6, 4, 6, 1, 9, -0.5 ] );
const X = new Complex128Array( [ 5, 1.5, 6, 4, 6, 1, 9, -0.5 ] );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 2 * n );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( n );
const FERR = new Float64Array( 1 );
const BERR = new Float64Array( 1 );

zgttrf.ndarray( n, DLF, 1, 0, DF, 1, 0, DUF, 1, 0, DU2, 1, 0, IPIV, 1, 0 );
zgttrs.ndarray( 'no-transpose', n, 1, DLF, 1, 0, DF, 1, 0, DUF, 1, 0, DU2, 1, 0, IPIV, 1, 0, X, 2, n * 2, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
const info = zgtrfs.ndarray( 'no-transpose', n, 1, DL, 1, 0, d, 1, 0, DU, 1, 0, DLF, 1, 0, DF, 1, 0, DUF, 1, 0, DU2, 1, 0, IPIV, 1, 0, B, 1, n, 0, X, 1, n, 0, FERR, 1, 0, BERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'X (Float64 view):', reinterpret( X, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'FERR:', FERR ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'BERR:', BERR ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZGTRFS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZGTRFS improves the computed solution to a system of linear equations when the coefficient matrix is tridiagonal, and provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution.

</section>
